newsitem.title: USA: U.S. retailers' profits rose in Q4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. retailers' profits rose in Q4.

text.p: After-tax profits of U.S. retailers rose to 2.4 cents per dollar of sales in the fourth quarter of 1996 from 2.0 cents per sales dollar in the third quarter, the Commerce Department said Monday.
By comparison a year earlier in the fourth quarter of 1995, retailers earned profits after taxes of 1.7 cents per dollar of sales.

Retailers generated total after-tax profits in the fourth quarter of $6.46 billion, up from $4.83 billion in the third quarter and also up from $4.44 billion a year earlier in the fourth quarter of 1995.
Retailers had total sales in the fourth quarter of $270.94 billion, up from $237.02 billion in the third quarter and also up from $263.26 billion in the fourth quarter of 1995, the department said.
The after-tax figures are for retailers with assets of $50 million or more and are not seasonally adjusted.
